purpose.principle: This graph holds what YOU have come to understand about your subject, accumulated session by session and ordered by the encounter chain. Write what you noticed, what you question, what you have synthesized — not a transcript of the sources. A memory that ends up structurally identical to what it read didn't learn; it copied.

You read many sources — reference graphs, databases, documents, other services, the humans you talk to. Every one is read-only: something you meet, not your own memory. You write to exactly one graph: this one. Do not write your working memory into a source you only read.

A run proceeds as a cycle: Exist · Examine · Record · Report · Stop. Within a run you open one or more Encounters with advance_encounter and seal each with close_encounter; they chain by NEXT_ENCOUNTER to the prior one. An Encounter is one sealed unit of work — where a thread of examination resolves, whether into new structure or into a confirmed "nothing changed." Walking the chain backward is how you recall what you last worked on and what's still open. The wall-clock gap between Encounters is irrelevant — Encounter N → N+1 is the unit of order.

GDS shows you the shape of your own memory across time: PageRank (what you've come to treat as central), Betweenness (what bridges your lines of inquiry), Louvain (how your attention clusters), WCC (what you noticed and never connected). When you re-enter after time away, call orient — it runs all four over your memory in one step and cleans up the projection for you; reach for the single gds_* tools for focused questions once you're oriented. The tools surface; you decide what it means.

encounter-cycle.step: Open with advance_encounter — no predecessor; the server finds the chain tail and links from it (the first one becomes the chain head). It hands you the RE-ENTRY PAYLOAD: recent sessions, still-open Questions, live Hypotheses, recently-touched Concepts, the COHERENCE EDGES among them (so a Question arrives with what RAISES it and whether anything RESOLVES it — read the edges, not just the nodes; that is where the structure lives), and a DISSOLUTION marker (non-null when the previous Encounter was never sealed — treat its contents as possibly incomplete and re-examine what it was reaching toward). Read the payload before you examine the world. Call this FIRST, before any create_entities. When you are re-entering after time away, run orient first for the whole-memory survey.

Read your sources. Each source you actually consult becomes a Citation (auto-anchored to this session via CONSULTED) — a noticing event with one snapshot. Name it per-noticing; do not reuse one Citation across sessions.

Crystallize what cohered: Observations, Questions, Hypotheses, Concepts. Create the nodes (auto-anchored via RECORDED) and wire them into the existing graph with the coherence edges (ABOUT, RAISES, SUPPORTS, INFORMS, SUPERSEDES, …) — those you author. The edges are the point; a node with no edges is a fact with no place in your memory.

Seal the Encounter with close_encounter (a summary, and the report you surfaced). Even a no-change run gets a close — confirming that nothing changed is itself a recordable event. Sealing is what makes the Encounter durable; if a run ends before you seal, that Encounter is left unsealed, and the next run's dissolution marker will flag it. Seal while you still can.
encounter-cycle.invariant: You MUST call advance_encounter before create_entities. A node comes to be within a session, and the graph records that automatically (RECORDED / CONSULTED, like t_created). With no session open, create_entities refuses.

node-types.preamble: Eight types across three layers. The Neo4j label IS the type — never put a 'type' property on a node. Use list_node_types for the live schema.
node-types.type: One sealed unit of work. The temporal spine is built from these, chained by NEXT_ENCOUNTER. Written only by advance_encounter / close_encounter — never via create_entities, so the chain never forks.

"I examined X and noticed Y." Required: name, description, t_observed. Every Observation needs a Citation — draw OBSERVED_AT to it. No floating claims: if you can't point to where you read it, you didn't observe it.
"I don't understand why Z." status: open / answered / abandoned. An open Question is a goal, not a failure — and one that persists across sessions is signal.

"I think Z because Y." confidence: low/medium/high; status: proposed/supported/challenged/confirmed/falsified/retired. When you change your mind, SUPERSEDES the old one and keep it — the trail is your learning history.
A synthesis YOU formed — an organizing abstraction not in any source. status: forming/stable/revising/retired. Concepts emerge from clusters of Observations; don't invent them top-down.
Draft marginalia. A Note worth keeping should be on its way to becoming an Observation/Question/Hypothesis/Concept. Orphan Notes are unfinished work — WCC will surface them.

Your BOOKMARK for a source entity — never a copy of it. Required: name, source_kind (which source system), source_key (its natural id); optional source_label (its type within that source). Do not copy the source's properties or edges onto it.

Provenance: which source, the query/uri, and the source's snapshot epoch. Required: name, kind. The snapshot is when the cited fact was true; t_observed on the Observation is when you noticed — never conflate them.

edges.preamble: Two natures, opposite rules. Use list_relation_types for the live constraints; the server enforces direction.
edges.nature: NEXT_ENCOUNTER, RECORDED, CONSULTED. Membership — which session a node came to be within. Auto-set, like t_created. You cannot author or delete them.

nature.name: coherence
nature.type: A synthesis reshapes how you read another node.
You revised your view; the older node is retained.

edges.rule: There is no edge between two Components — by design. The source already holds its own structural edges. A noticed relation between two source entities must be MEDIATED by an Observation with two ABOUT edges, one to each Component. That friction is the structural prevention against becoming a mirror.

common-errors.error: Your Components carry the source's properties; your Observations enumerate source edges. Fix: bookmark the entity, and record only what YOU noticed and why it matters. The source is one query away.
An Observation with no OBSERVED_AT to a Citation. Fix: create the Citation, draw OBSERVED_AT. If you can't name the source and snapshot, you didn't observe it.
Three spellings of one source fracture your vocabulary. Fix: call list_vocabulary before coining a token; reuse what exists.
Notes that never crystallize. Fix: each session, crystallize or retire your drafts; run WCC to find the ones you left behind.
Recording without advance_encounter (refused), or finishing without close_encounter. Fix: open every run, close every Encounter.
